raw_response:
I am old now, so I do not want to toss money around, but I also cannot let the peanut stand go weak. On my 4.1 mu, I will still plant peanut like usual. Peanut is what I know, and on such a small piece of land it is safer to keep doing what has worked. People nearby also say peanut is still manageable if you watch the weeds early and do not save too much on base fertilizer. I only finished primary school, so I do not count too finely. I look at the soil, the weather, and what happened last year.

This year at the start I will prepare the land well and plant around late April, when the ground is warm enough. I will use decent local improved seed, not the most expensive kind, because cash must stay in hand. Peanut does not need as much nitrogen as wheat or maize, but if the base manure or compound fertilizer is too little, the pods do not fill well. So I will put a moderate base fertilizer, then a small top-up later if the plants look weak. Since I have well water, I can irrigate if it stays dry, but pumping costs money, so I will probably water only about twice, mainly at flowering and pod-setting if rain is short. For labor, my family is small, so most work is still done by us, and if harvest comes all at once I may hire a little help for pulling and drying.
